Explanation:  
The Ground Truth Answer states that R. B. Bennett was the Prime Minister of Canada when the Toronto Maple Leafs first won the Stanley Cup. The Predicted Answer claims that Sir Robert Borden was the Prime Minister when the franchise won its first Stanley Cup in 1918, noting that the team was then known as the Toronto Arenas. 

Historically, the Toronto team won the Stanley Cup for the first time in 1918 as the Toronto Arenas, and Sir Robert Borden was indeed the Prime Minister at that time (1911–1920). The name "Maple Leafs" was adopted in 1927, and their first Stanley Cup as the "Toronto Maple Leafs" was in 1932, during which R. B. Bennett was the Prime Minister. 

The Ground Truth Answer interprets the question as referring to the first Stanley Cup as the "Toronto Maple Leafs" (1932), not as a franchise under previous names.

The Predicted Answer provides Borden as the Prime Minister when the franchise first won the cup, but it clarifies the team was not yet known as the Maple Leafs. It does not mention R. B. Bennett nor specify the 1932 win as "Maple Leafs." Therefore, the meaning and vital facts of the Ground Truth Answer are NOT present in the Predicted Answer.

Decision: FALSE
